Consequently every generic comparison path on YY between these endpoints has at least 3b3b smooth two-branch cover–time pairs carrying an odd kernel. For a sufficiently close generic perturbation of the short path, there are at least three such pairs in each of bb disjoint neighborhoods, one about each split nodal double joined at a ramification point of ff. The endpoints may be arbitrarily close to AA. This generic comparison allows the operator at the original central time to move.

The lower graph deformation sequence identifies both kernel and cokernel of AA with real lines, since the lower branch velocities together with time give an isomorphism. Its radial normal section σ=[(0,ξ)]\sigma=[(0,\xi)] has a double zero at each ramification and no other zero. The local expansion and the nonzero projected antilinear coefficient at each double zero are the calculation of Calculation F3, which takes place in a single ramification disk. The same note computes the local odd Euler change −3ηA-3\eta_A in the split root chart, separately at every one of these points.

We check the global regularity on the upper finite surface. Use variations on a regular lower disk annihilating ξ\xi as in Calculation F6. When the upper sign character and its translate by the lower involution τ\tau differ on the complement of their branch values, that argument gives transversality for the odd incidence. Its real projective index with moving branch positions is −4+4−1=−1-4+4-1=-1. The connected étale twists are regular using the same variations by Calculation E1.

If the upper double admits a lift of τ\tau and its distinct branch values form a nonfixed pair y,τyy,\tau y, the lift squares to the identity because of the fiber over a lower fixed point. The upper odd part splits into two eigensystems. At each of the bb lower fixed points its rank-two bundle at the Dolbeault reference, Nγ⊗L−1N^\gamma\otimes L^{-1} for the upper root LL, has one positive and one negative weight. Pullback of either eigendirect image thus has length-one quotient at each of those bb points. The degree of either rank-two eigendirect image on CC is 2h−4−b2=2g−3.\frac{2h-4-b}{2}=2g-3. Its real index is −2-2, the moving orbit has two real parameters, and projectivization again gives index −1-1. Paired-sheet testing supplies transversality in each eigensystem as in Calculation F6. For a divisor consisting of two distinct lower fixed points, a lift must square to the nontrivial upper deck by its action in the local square-root coordinate. When b>2b>2, the square fixes the two-point fiber over a third lower fixed point, a contradiction. The possible order-four case at b=2b=2 is covered in Calculation F6. This exhausts the distinct branch divisors.

On a nodal upper double with connected normalization the odd kernel embeds in a regular étale twist. On a split normalization an odd kernel is (aσ,−aσ)(a\sigma,-a\sigma) and matching requires aσ(y)=0a\sigma(y)=0. We have therefore identified the entire compact upper odd kernel incidence at time zero. At each exceptional point the local degree calculation also gives isolation as time varies through zero. This makes the endpoints regular throughout a sufficiently small punctured time interval, by compactness. The usual projective transversality arguments used here work first in finite differentiability. Openness away from the finite exceptional neighborhoods, and the local lower bound by the linear and conjugate-cubic terms of Calculation F3 inside them, give the smooth perturbations with the same conclusions. Equivalently one may work on a countable exhaustion of the smooth cover charts in the smooth parameter space, using localized finite-dimensional tensor variations and ordinary parametric transversality. For the smooth count use unrestricted real fixed-symbol perturbations on YY. With the index-zero twist, real projectivization, time and yy, the projection index is 0−1+1+2−4=−20-1+1+2-4=-2. The compact surface and regular endpoints give finiteness. The signed count is the endpoint odd Euler difference along every such path by Calculation E5. Examples over one genus-two curve. For each j≥1j\ge1 the change of positive orthogonal axes by degree offset 2j2j in Calculation E5 has nonzero top ordinary crossing count in genus h=4+2jh=4+2j. Transversality with a prescribed graph

G1. Kernels on imprimitive quartic covers at a prescribed double wall

As in Calculation E1, there is a disk of regular lower values with a sheet of nonzero height ss on which Bs∉ℂsB s\notin\mathbb C s. In fact s=zv+O(|z|2)s=zv+O(|z|^2) in w=c+z2w=c+z^2, so this assertion holds above sufficiently small nonzero w−cw-c. Fix a relatively compact subdisk with this property.

Use smooth real zeroth-order variations supported in the closure of this subdisk and annihilating the real vector ss pointwise. Theorem. For a residual set of such perturbations, simultaneously in every source genus, let u:X→Cu:X\to C be a connected finite holomorphic cover with smooth source. Every connected degree-three cover has zero kernel for the same residual set. The ramification indices and coincidences of branch values of uu are unrestricted.

Equivariant operator and branch parameters

Its kernel is Hom⁡G(V,ker⁡π*D)\operatorname{Hom}_G(V,\ker\pi^*D). It is Fredholm on W1,p→LpW^{1,p}\to L^p, p>2p>2, by the finite group projections on the two Banach spaces. Then ind⁡ℝDV=−2∑c(dim⁡ℝV−dim⁡ℝVIc).\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}D_V =-2\sum_c\big(\dim_{\mathbb R}V-\dim_{\mathbb R}V^{I_c}\big). \tag{2} For the index, homotope to a pulled-back Dolbeault operator. The direct image on CC of the equivariant complex is the Dolbeault cohomology of N⊗EVN\otimes E_V, where EV=(π*𝒪X̃⊗ℝV*)GE_V=(\pi_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde X}\otimes_{\mathbb R}V^*)^G. Its pulled-back evaluation into the trivial bundle with fiber Vℂ*V^*_{\mathbb C} is an isomorphism off ramification. At an inertia group of order ee, write w=zew=z^e and diagonalize a generator. The invariant generators in an eigenbasis are zjieiz^{j_i}e_i for the required residues 0≤ji<e0\le j_i<e. Riemann–Roch for the rank 2k2k bundle N⊗EVN\otimes E_V gives (2). This argument also covers a real representation of complex type. Equivariant pullback operators, Bai–Swaminathan, §2.1.

On a fixed monodromy stratum let rr be the number of distinct branch values of the Galois cover. The stratum has rr complex parameters. Locally mark the values, transport their monodromies by an isotopy, cover the complementary punctured surface, and fill in with z↦zez\mapsto z^e at each puncture. This construction gives all nearby covers of that type by uniqueness of the holomorphic extension. There are only finitely many monodromy homomorphisms to a fixed GG for fixed marked branch data. In particular two ramification points over one value in a given stratum contribute one moving value there. If VV is faithful, every one of these rr inertia groups acts nontrivially, so ind⁡ℝDV+2r−1≤−1.\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}D_V+2r-1\le -1. \tag{3} The subtraction by one projectivizes a nonzero real solution. If an inertia group is invisible in a representation, one can instead form the operator and the parameter count on its faithful quotient cover. This distinction is needed for the intermediate double characters.

The test on a regular disk

We prove surjectivity of the universal projective kernel equation in the cases needed for (1). Suppose VV is a faithful real plane, or is the sign line of a double different from ff. A nonzero equivariant solution is an injective real GG-map from VV into the space of global solutions on X̃\widetilde X, by irreducibility. Choose a real basis, and denote its images by u1,u2u_1,u_2 in the plane case and by u1u_1 in the line case. Form a connected common Galois cover of X̃\widetilde X and YY, using the intersection of the monodromy kernels on the complement of their branch divisors and normalizing over the removed points. The lifted solution space contains the irreducible VV-module spanned by the uiu_i and the lower sign line spanned by ss (globally, the pullback of ξ\xi). These modules are inequivalent. For two double monodromies, equivalent sign characters on the common punctured curve would give the same completed double cover. Consequently s,u1s,u_1 or s,u1,u2s,u_1,u_2, as applicable, are linearly independent global solutions over ℝ\mathbb R.

In the fixed testing disk choose a smaller disk missing the branch values of this cover. Identify one lift with the disk. If u1=asu_1=a s throughout an open disk there, for a complex-valued coefficient aa, the product rule modulo ℂs\mathbb C s gives (a‾−a)[Bs]=0(\bar a-a)[Bs]=0. Thus aa is real and ∂‾a=0\bar\partial a=0. Unique continuation would give a global constant dependence. There is therefore a subdisk on which s,u1s,u_1 are complex independent. In the plane case, if u2=as+bu1u_2=a s+b u_1 throughout this subdisk for real functions a,ba,b, these functions are smooth and the real Leibniz rule gives (∂‾a)s+(∂‾b)u1=0(\bar\partial a)s+(\bar\partial b)u_1=0. Complex independence forces both to be constant, again contradicting unique continuation. On a further disk the three displayed vectors are pointwise real independent.

An arbitrary smooth real tensor supported on this disk and killing ss can therefore prescribe arbitrary smooth compactly supported images of the one or two vectors uiu_i. Choose a smooth complement to their real span together with ss to extend the prescription. Testing an adjoint annihilator of the universal derivative with these tensors kills the adjoint on this lift. Indeed its equivariant coefficient has one value in the dual slot for each chosen basis element, and the pairings summed over deck translates on the Galois cover are equal by equivariance and the invariant inner product. Variation of the section in the invariant domain gives the homogeneous adjoint equation, since projecting any test to its invariant part preserves its pairing with the equivariant adjoint. Unique continuation kills the adjoint everywhere on the connected Galois cover. The cokernel of the section derivative is finite dimensional, so the universal derivative is onto. Projectivizing preserves transversality at a zero by real homogeneity. For a cyclic plane this argument uses two real basis elements even though its commuting algebra is complex.

Apply Sard–Smale to this universal equation on each smooth stratum. After fixing a smooth identification of the Galois covers locally, the branch parameters occur in a smooth family of elliptic operators, using sufficiently high finite differentiability for the perturbations. The projective projection has index (3), so a generic perturbation has no solution in the indicated representation on that stratum. To pass to the smooth topology, exhaust each stratum away from the excluded lower double (where relevant) by countably many compact subsets of its charts. Absence of a kernel on a compact subset is open by uniform elliptic stabilization. It is dense by the finite-differentiability result at arbitrarily high regularity and smooth approximation within the bundle of allowed tensors. For a fixed number of branch values and a fixed finite group there are countably many charts and monodromy data; taking their countable intersection also permits all numbers of branch values at once. This gives the claimed residual set. The argument is local on the smooth strata and does not assert uniform estimates over a sequence of unbounded genera.

Constituents and pullback through the prescribed double

Let GG be the monodromy of a smooth connected dd-sheeted map, acting faithfully on its sheets, and HH a sheet stabilizer. Pullback identifies a downstairs homogeneous solution with an HH-invariant solution on the Galois closure. For the converse, invariance gives descent off the ramification points of the map to XX; boundedness and elliptic removability extend the descended solution. By finite group reciprocity the only possible irreducibles contributing to these HH-fixed vectors are the constituents of ℝ[G/H]\mathbb R[G/H].

For an imprimitive quartic the transitive group preserves a partition into two pairs and embeds in the symmetries of a square. Its order is divisible by four and divides eight. At order four its action is regular and it is cyclic or Klein four. At order eight it is the dihedral group of order eight acting on the four vertices. The constituents are as follows, with 𝟏\mathbf1 the trivial summand.

Monodromy Permutation representation
C4C_4 𝟏\mathbf1, its unique nontrivial sign, and the faithful rotation plane
C2×C2C_2\times C_2 𝟏\mathbf1 and the three nontrivial signs
D4D_4 of order eight 𝟏\mathbf1, the sign of the exchange of the two blocks, and the faithful plane

For the dihedral row, functions constant on each block give the first two summands. The differences within each block span the plane, on which the independent sign changes and interchange of the two coordinates act faithfully and irreducibly. The trivial part has zero kernel by the base hypothesis. Each nontrivial sign in the table descends to its own quadratic quotient, so it is tested on the family of that quotient using only the branch values at which its sign is negative. Formula (2) gives index −2r-2r there. Projectivization thus gives index −1-1 whatever the number of branch values, including zero. The disk test excludes all of these kernels except on the specified double ff. In the faithful plane the full quartic branch locus is visible; (2) charges a reflection one complex parameter and a nonidentity rotation two. Thus (3) applies even when ramification over a given point is not simple. In degree three the transitive groups are C3C_3 and S3S_3. Their permutation representations both consist of 𝟏\mathbf1 and a faithful irreducible real plane, so the same argument proves the cubic assertion.

A sign from ff is a summand with HH-fixed vectors precisely when HH is contained in its kernel in the monodromy quotient. This is exactly the criterion that the map from XX lift through YY over CC, by applying the covering criterion off the union of the branch divisors and extending over the punctures. When this occurs, its solution line is the descended pullback of ξ\xi and all other summands have zero kernel. This proves (1).

For a connected nodal stable map of total degree four whose positive normalizations have degrees at most three or are imprimitive quartics, restrictions to the positive normalizations are now determined by (1) and the cubic assertion. Each nonzero positive section is a real multiple of the pullback of ξ\xi. On a contracted normalization the section is constant, and the remaining equations are equality of the values at the two flags of each node. Thus these maps have precisely the positive images considered in Calculation E2 whenever they carry a nonzero section. A primitive quartic normalization has monodromy A4A_4 or S4S_4 and its nontrivial constituent has real dimension three; the preceding disk test treats dimensions one and two.

G2. Kernels on primitive quartic covers at a prescribed double wall

Let CC be a closed Riemann surface of genus g≥2g\ge 2, and let NN be a complex plane bundle of degree 2g−22g-2. Let DD be a real Cauchy–Riemann operator on NN, invertible on CC. Fix a connected branched double f:Y→Cf:Y\to C with ker⁡f*D=ℝξ\ker f^*D=\mathbb R\xi odd. Suppose there is a disk UU of regular values on which one height ss is nonzero and Bs∉ℂsBs\notin\mathbb C s, in a coordinate trivializing the form factor of the antilinear term BB of DD. At a simple ramification point with w=c+z2w=c+z^2, ξ=zv+O(|z|2)\xi=zv+O(|z|^2) and B(c)v∉ℂvB(c)v\notin\mathbb Cv, every sufficiently close regular value has this property. Take smooth real zeroth-order variations supported in U¯\overline U which annihilate ss pointwise. They also annihilate −s-s on the other sheet. Work in a sufficiently small neighborhood of DD so that the disk condition persists on a fixed smaller disk, the base remains invertible, and the lower kernel stays simple. If the given double wall is transverse in a path, these variations may be inserted with a time cutoff while preserving transversality.

Proposition. For a residual set of these variations the pullback operator on every smooth connected primitive quartic cover of CC is injective, simultaneously in all source genera. Consequently on any smooth connected cover u:X→Cu:X\to C of degree at most four the kernel is zero unless u=fpu=fp. In that case it is the line ℝp*ξ\mathbb R p^*\xi.

The second assertion also follows by adjoining the imprimitive, cubic and double cases of Calculation G1. We prove the dimension-three assertion directly, including the test on adjoints which is needed when the three quartic heights and the prescribed lower height are pointwise real dependent.

Twisted equation. Let VV be an irreducible orthogonal real representation of finite monodromy on a punctured CC, of dimension k≤3k\le3. Fill in the punctures with trivial monodromy. The normalized connected Galois cover of the remaining punctured curve with group the monodromy image has a compactification π:Z→C\pi:Z\to C by the local power maps. On ZZ, apply π*D\pi^*D to GG-equivariant VV-valued sections of π*N\pi^*N. Equivalently, use the twist DVD_V on the orbifold CνC_\nu whose isotropy orders are the orders of the local monodromies. On a regular disk the equation in a parallel orthonormal frame of VV is DD on each coefficient. In particular a nonzero kernel gives a GG-equivariant map from VV to the space of solutions on the connected regular cover, injective by irreducibility.

For an actual finite cover, take its permutation local system on the complement of its branch values. The orbifold pushforward of the trivial real local system splits orthogonally into its irreducible summands, and the twisted operator splits accordingly. Its kernel identifies with the ordinary pullback kernel on the smooth source. Indeed the lifts of solutions satisfy the equation in the power charts. In the reverse direction invariant solutions descend away from the branch locus, are bounded there, and extend on the coarse source by removal of singularities for its ordinary smooth real Cauchy–Riemann operator. This argument concerns solutions. The adjoints below are taken in the invariant complex on ZZ with its smooth invariant densities; all coefficient pairings are made away from the branch locus. Doan–Walpuski, proof of Proposition 2.8.5.

Let χ\chi be the lower sign local system. To compare VV and χ\chi, remove the union of their branch loci and use the connected regular cover of this complement for the intersection of the two monodromy kernels. Restriction to this cover means pulling both solutions back to the same equation; the deck group maps onto the monodromy group of each system. Suppose VV and χ\chi are inequivalent representations of this common deck group. If t1,…,tkt_1,\ldots,t_k are the coefficients of a nonzero DVD_V-solution in a parallel orthonormal basis, the k+1k+1 sections s,t1,…,tks,t_1,\ldots,t_k are linearly independent over the real constants on each test disk. Indeed the equivariant maps from χ\chi and from VV into the solution space are injective and have disjoint images, and a constant relation on a disk extends throughout the connected regular cover by unique continuation. This applies also when ramification values of the two systems coincide.

Testing the two sides of the tensor. Choose a disk inside the allowed support, disjoint from the two branch loci, on which Bs∉ℂsBs\notin\mathbb Cs. If t1=ast_1=a s everywhere there with aa complex, applying DD modulo ℂs\mathbb C s gives (a‾−a)[Bs]=0(\bar a-a)[Bs]=0. Hence aa is real and (∂‾a)s=0(\bar\partial a)s=0, contrary to independence over the constants. Thus there is a subdisk on which s,t1s,t_1 are independent over ℂ\mathbb C. For k≥2k\ge2, if t2=as+bt1t_2=a s+b t_1 throughout this disk with real a,ba,b, the coefficients are smooth and the equation gives (∂‾a)s+(∂‾b)t1=0(\bar\partial a)s+(\bar\partial b)t_1=0. Both would be constant. On a further subdisk s,t1,t2s,t_1,t_2 are therefore independent over ℝ\mathbb R. With P:Nℝ→Nℝ/ℝsP:N_{\mathbb R}\to N_{\mathbb R}/\mathbb Rs and T:V→NℝT:V\to N_{\mathbb R} the coefficient evaluation ej↦tje_j\mapsto t_j, we have obtained rank⁡(PT)≥min⁡(k,2)\operatorname{rank}(PT)\ \ge\ \min(k,2) on a nonempty open disk.

At a solution consider a covector annihilating the section and allowed operator derivatives of DVt=0D_Vt=0. The section derivative gives the homogeneous adjoint equation. Projectivizing the kernel line makes no difference to this test, since the omitted vector is already in the kernel. An invariant annihilator on ZZ satisfies the ordinary adjoint equation there, by averaging arbitrary test sections. Write its coefficients on the disk as pjp_j in the real dual of the form fiber F=Λ0,1T*C⊗ℂNF=\Lambda^{0,1}T^*C\otimes_{\mathbb C}N, using one common positive base density. In this description the coefficients solve the same local dual equation. Tracing the pairings on all sheets gives a common positive factor times ∫∑j=1kpj(Atj)\int \sum_{j=1}^k p_j(A t_j) for each allowed operator variation AA. Indeed on any other lift the two coefficient arrays are transformed by the same orthogonal matrix, which leaves the contraction invariant. Expressing all dual densities relative to the lifted base density on this disk accounts for its coordinate Jacobian. The available AA are precisely the compactly supported smooth maps factoring through PP. If Q:V→Fℝ*Q:V\to F^*_{\mathbb R} sends eje_j to pjp_j, pointwise tensor duality gives (PT)Q⊤=0,Q⊤:Fℝ→V.(PT)Q^\top=0,\qquad Q^\top:F_{\mathbb R}\longrightarrow V. For k≤2k\le2 this forces Q=0Q=0. For k=3k=3 it gives rank⁡Q≤1\operatorname{rank}Q\le1 on the disk. A nonzero adjoint would give an injective equivariant map from VV to the dual solutions on the connected regular cover, again by irreducibility. On a subdisk where p1≠0p_1\ne0 the rank bound would then give p2=ap1p_2=a p_1 for a smooth real function aa. The adjoint product rule gives σD†(da)p1=0\sigma_{D^\dagger}(da)p_1=0; ellipticity forces da=0da=0. Unique continuation contradicts the independence of the two adjoint solutions. Thus in all cases the annihilator is zero. The section derivative has closed image of finite codimension, so the universal derivative is onto. This uses neither pointwise independence of all four heights nor regularity of any adjoint divided by a base differential at a branch value.

Dimension and genericity. Let rr be the number of distinct branch values of the faithful monodromy cover of VV, and let IxI_x denote the inertia group at xx. The real index of the twisted equation is ind⁡ℝDV=−2∑x(k−dim⁡ℝVIx).\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}D_V =-2\sum_x\bigl(k-\dim_{\mathbb R}V^{I_x}\bigr). Here ind⁡ℝD=0\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}D=0 and rk⁡ℂN=2\operatorname{rk}_{\mathbb C}N=2. This is the orbifold index formula, also computed from the invariant direct image in Calculation G1. The faithfulness convention ensures that every displayed summand is at least one. Ordering and moving the rr distinct values gives rr complex parameters in the fixed monodromy stratum. Projectivization by real scaling gives incidence index at most 2r−2r−1=−12r-2r-1=-1 over the allowed perturbations. Values of a larger cover where VV has trivial inertia are absent from this count; its twisted kernel descends across those values. Doan–Walpuski, Propositions 2.8.5–2.8.6.

In each relatively compact smooth Hurwitz chart use normalized solutions before dividing by sign. Over a compact subset of the chart their set at a fixed operator is compact by the uniform elliptic estimates on the smooth family of compact Galois covers. At each such solution the surjectivity just proved uses finitely many smooth allowed tensors in addition to the section variables. Finitely many such neighborhoods suffice, and surjectivity persists there. Elliptic compactness puts all solutions over the compact subset for nearby operators in these neighborhoods. Ordinary parametric transversality in the resulting finite-dimensional family gives density of operators without kernels over this compact subset, and compactness gives openness. Compact chart exhaustions, ramification types and finite monodromy representations form a countable collection up to equivalence. Its Baire intersection proves the assertion for all VV inequivalent to χ\chi of dimension at most three. In passing to the faithful monodromy chart, equivalence to χ\chi is a closed condition (its branch divisor must equal that of ff, and the remaining monodromy is discrete). The complement is exhausted by compact subsets as above.

For a transitive quartic cover the permutation space is ℝ𝟏⊕𝟏⟂\mathbb R\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf1^\perp with dim⁡ℝ𝟏⟂=3\dim_{\mathbb R}\mathbf1^\perp=3. For primitive monodromy the group is A4A_4 or S4S_4 and 𝟏⟂\mathbf1^\perp is irreducible: A4A_4 has no nontrivial real sign character, the sum-zero space has no fixed vector, and an invariant proper subspace would give an invariant line by orthogonality. The base summand is invertible. This proves primitive injectivity. For every transitive permutation representation of degree at most four all the remaining irreducibles likewise have dimension at most three. The lower character occurs exactly when the sheet stabilizer on the common punctured base lies in ker⁡χ\ker\chi, and then with multiplicity one: a sign-equivariant function on the sheets is determined by one value and exists precisely under this stabilizer condition. The resulting covering map to the lower double extends across the punctures by the local power models. The χ\chi-kernel is then the given odd line. This proves the proposition.

Paths. In the space of unrestricted fixed-symbol paths relative to regular endpoints, a generic path has no simultaneous simply ramified double wall with the disk condition above and a nonzero kernel on a twist V≄χV\not\simeq\chi of real rank at most three. Indeed, use two separate Hurwitz and section variables and a common variation of DD. On the joint incidence, testing first with variations killing the current ss forces the second adjoint to vanish by the disk argument. Then arbitrary tensors on a regular disk test the lower odd adjoint, whose pairing with AsAs vanishes for every AA only if that adjoint vanishes. The two equations are therefore jointly regular. The lower projectivized incidence has index −1-1 over operators at a simply ramified double, and the other incidence has index at most −1-1. Adding the common time still leaves negative index. Countable relative transversality gives the stated avoidance. For a prescribed central crossing one can instead make the graph-preserving perturbation in the proposition.

There is also a restriction on smooth primitive quartic crossings along an unrestricted generic path at times where the base operator is invertible. In the preceding tensor test one may now take P=1P=1. Two coefficients of a nonzero standard solution are real independent on a subdisk: real proportionality on a disk where the first is nonzero would force a constant ratio. Thus rank⁡T≥2\operatorname{rank}T\ge2 there and the same adjoint argument proves universal regularity. Write ρx\rho_x for the permutation around a distinct branch value xx and dx=4−#cycles(ρx)d_x=4-\#\mathrm{cycles}(\rho_x), counting fixed letters as cycles. Its fixed space on the standard summand has codimension dxd_x. The projectivized incidence along the path has index −2∑x(dx−1)-2\sum_x(d_x-1). Hence every such crossing has only simple branching at distinct values, or is unramified, and each kernel is a real line since the regular incidence is zero-dimensional. With positive branching the primitive group must be S4S_4. These conclusions concern smooth finite covers. A compactified moduli space also includes nodal maps, for which the normalization kernels must satisfy the separate matching conditions.

G3. Kernels on finite covers with one prescribed double graph

Let CC be a closed Riemann surface of genus g≥2g\ge2, N→CN\to C a complex rank-two bundle of degree 2g−22g-2, and DD a smooth real Cauchy–Riemann operator with its usual complex symbol. Fix a connected double f:Y→Cf:Y\to C and an odd section ξ≠0\xi\ne0 such that ker⁡f*D=ℝξ\ker f^*D=\mathbb R\xi, ker⁡D=0\ker D=0. Suppose the lower branch and time derivatives give a transverse crossing for a chosen path. For an unramified double the transverse derivative consists of the time column alone. Let V⋐CV\Subset C be a disk of regular values with nonzero lower sheet height on its closure. On this disk choose one sheet and use ξ\xi also for its section of NN. The opposite sheet has height −ξ-\xi. Perturb DD by smooth real zeroth-order tensors supported in a fixed compact subset of VV with nonempty interior, annihilating ξ\xi there. Work in a small open neighborhood where the base invertibility, simple prescribed kernel and transverse crossing persist. A cutoff in time incorporates the perturbation in the original path.

Theorem. For a residual set of these perturbations, simultaneously for every smooth connected finite cover a:X→Ca:X\to C of arbitrary degree and genus, ker⁡a*D={ℝp*ξif a=fp for a holomorphic p:X→Y,0otherwise.\ker a^*D= \begin{cases} \mathbb R\,p^*\xi & \text{if }a=fp\text{ for a holomorphic }p:X\to Y,\\ 0 & \text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \tag{1} We denote the perturbed operator also by DD. The two choices of a lift pp in the first line exchange the sign of its generator. The argument applies to both ramified and unramified doubles. The assertion is residual at the prescribed graph. It gives no single open interval of neighboring operators that works in all degrees.

The local input is Wendl’s infinite-jet Petri theorem in the formulation of Doan and Walpuski. We explain how to use unrestricted jets when allowed variations annihilate a fixed nonzero solution. The argument below works on any test subdisk on which that solution is nonzero. Doan–Walpuski, Definition 1.6.3 and Theorems 1.6.17, 2.5.3 · Wendl, Corollary 5.10.

A Petri jet in the constrained space

For the real operator on the regular disk the infinite-jet condition at xx says that multiplication of formal solution and formal adjoint-solution jets is injective on their algebraic real tensor product. The adjoint uses the dual bundle with density values; thus the condition is invariant under smooth complex bundle gauge, using the corresponding output gauge and the dual change of variables for the adjoint. In the space of unrestricted smooth zeroth-order perturbations of a fixed Cauchy–Riemann symbol, operators with this condition at a chosen xx are dense. Indeed localized smooth perturbations realize every finite jet, and that symbol satisfies Wendl’s condition. One can use the smooth-coefficient Banach parameter neighborhoods in the cited theorem inside any prescribed finite set of smooth-norm tolerances.

Fix xx in the interior of the support region and a smaller disk about xx. Choose an unrestricted nearby operator D′D' with a Petri jet there. It has a local solution s′s' close to ξ\xi on a still smaller disk. In a complex trivialization write D′=∂‾+M′D'=\bar\partial+M', with M′M' real linear. On a sufficiently small disk the Cauchy transform composed with multiplication by M′M' has sup operator norm less than one, uniformly for D′D' near DD. Solving D′(s′−ξ)=−D′ξD'(s'-\xi)=-D'\xi by this inverse gives the sup estimate, and interior elliptic estimates give arbitrary prescribed finite-order closeness on a smaller disk by taking D′D' sufficiently close. The solution is smooth. Choose a complex-linear covector field ll with l(ξ)=1l(\xi)=1. Then G=1+(s′−ξ)⊗lG=1+(s'-\xi)\otimes l is a smooth complex gauge close to the identity sending ξ\xi to s′s'. The operator G−1D′GG^{-1}D'G has the original symbol, the required Petri jet at xx, and annihilates ξ\xi. Its difference from DD now annihilates ξ\xi pointwise. Multiply that difference by a cutoff supported in the construction disk and equal to one near xx. This yields the asserted density of a good jet at this point by allowed smooth perturbations. Only this density is used.

A constrained adjoint test

Choose an irreducible real orthogonal finite-monodromy local system WW on the complement of a finite set of points of CC. At the punctures use the orbifold extensions of orders equal to the orders of the respective monodromies. Omit every point where that monodromy is trivial. The corresponding twisted operator is the equivariant operator on a finite smooth normal cover, or equivalently the operator on orbifold sections. Assume WW differs from the sign system of ff after passing to the common punctured curve. A connected compact normal cover dominating the two systems is obtained from the kernel of their joint finite representation and normalization across the punctures. The trivial system is harmless by base invertibility.

Let s≠0s\ne0 be an orbifold solution of DWD^W. In a real orthonormal flat frame over a regular test disk write s=(s1,…,sr)s=(s_1,\ldots,s_r), where r=rank⁡ℝWr=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb R}W. On the common normal cover these components are the images of a basis under a nonzero equivariant map from W*W^* to the real solution space. Its kernel is an invariant subspace, so it is injective. The prescribed lower solution transforms by a different irreducible character. Hence s1,…,sr,ξs_1,\ldots,s_r,\xi are real linearly independent on the common cover. Any real linear relation on their infinite jets at a chosen regular point is a solution vanishing to infinite order, hence vanishes everywhere by strong unique continuation. Their jets there are real linearly independent.

Suppose an adjoint η\eta annihilates the derivative of the kernel equation on nonzero sections under all allowed operator variations and all section variations. The latter imply (DW)†η=0(D^W)^\dagger\eta=0. On a test disk disjoint from the punctures η\eta is smooth with components η1,…,ηr\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r. Testing against localized real tensors KK with Kξ=0K\xi=0 gives the pointwise real tensor identity ∑i=1rsi⊗ηi=ξ⊗α\sum_{i=1}^r s_i\otimes\eta_i=\xi\otimes\alpha for some smooth dual output density α\alpha. This is the annihilator of the subspace of maps vanishing on ξ\xi. The right-hand factor is itself a local adjoint solution. In fact let Φ\Phi be any smooth compactly supported complex-linear endomorphism of NN on this disk. Its action on the output also acts trivially on the cotangent factor. Its commutator with DD is zeroth order by complex linearity of the symbol. Pair the identity with this commutator. On the left, ∑i∫⟨ηi,[D,Φ]si⟩=∑i∫⟨ηi,D(Φsi)⟩=0.\sum_i\int\langle\eta_i,[D,\Phi]s_i\rangle =\sum_i\int\langle\eta_i,D(\Phi s_i)\rangle=0. The right side gives ∫⟨α,D(Φξ)⟩=0\int\langle\alpha,D(\Phi\xi)\rangle=0. The fields Φξ\Phi\xi include every compactly supported smooth section of NN on the disk, by the same complex covector ll used above. Thus D†α=0D^\dagger\alpha=0 there. The commutator need not be an allowed perturbation; it tests a tensor identity already established using the allowed ones.

At a Petri jet in this disk the last pointwise relation induces a zero element in the tensor product of the formal solution and adjoint solution spaces. The independence of the input jets implies that each ηi\eta_i has zero infinite jet. Adjoint strong unique continuation on the connected normal cover gives η=0\eta=0. This proves surjectivity of the universal equation at such an operator and nonzero solution. Equivariance is accounted for by contraction in the flat frame. The proof uses real projectivization, which suffices also for irreducibles of complex or quaternionic type.

Moving the effective branch points

Consider a marked chart of systems of this fixed finite representation type with exactly s0s_0 effective punctures. Their distinct positions are its only continuous parameters, of real dimension 2s02s_0. Over a small simply connected configuration chart the finite normal covers form a smooth family, by the prescribed monodromy and the local maps z↦zez\mapsto z^e. For local monodromy IxI_x put cx=r−dim⁡ℝWIxc_x=r-\dim_{\mathbb R}W^{I_x}. The real Fredholm index is ind⁡ℝDW=−2∑xcx.\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}D^W=-2\sum_x c_x. For example, deform to a complex-linear reference. In a local inertia eigenframe of WℂW_{\mathbb C} of order ee the exponents of the invariant direct image pair as k,e−kk,e-k on the nonreal eigenvalues and equal e/2e/2 for −1-1. Their sum is ecx/2e c_x/2. Pullback of this direct image on the normal cover therefore has total degree loss |G|cx/2|G|c_x/2 over xx, where GG is its finite monodromy group. The smooth direct image of invariant sections at the Dolbeault reference has degree −∑cx/2-\sum c_x/2 in the flat factor. Tensor with the index-zero rank-two bundle on CC and apply Riemann–Roch. This gives the displayed real index, including the unramified case. It is also Doan–Walpuski, Proposition 2.8.6.

Including the branch positions and removing the real scalar gives projection index 2s0−1−2∑xcx≤−1,2s_0-1-2\sum_x c_x\le-1, \tag{2} since every retained monodromy acts nontrivially. Punctures visible to a larger cover but invisible to this representation play no role. Projectivize locally by a normalization transverse to the kernel scaling; the discarded radial direction maps to zero in the linearized equation.

Here are the topology details connecting the jet test with (2). Use countably many relatively compact subcharts in the configuration spaces and finite monodromy data, with compact exhaustions. Distinct finite groups and their real irreducibles, and homomorphisms from each finitely generated punctured surface group to a finite group, constitute countably many choices up to equivalence. For systems that could equal the character of ff, remove the data actually equal to that system before taking the compact exhaustions. The equality condition there fixes its branch positions and discrete monodromy, hence is closed in its fixed smooth chart. Refine the charts so that each compact block of branch configurations misses a test subdisk in the interior of the chosen variation support. This is possible locally at every configuration of finitely many points.

For each block absence of a kernel is open by compactness and elliptic estimates on the smooth family of normal covers. To prove density, begin at any operator in the small constrained neighborhood and insert a good Petri jet at an xx on that block’s test disk, as above. At this smooth operator the normalized solutions over the compact block form a compact set; one may use unit L2L^2 normalization in smooth local bundle identifications. All universal kernel equations there are surjective by the adjoint test. Finitely many smooth allowed tensor directions suffice on neighborhoods covering this compact set, by finite-dimensional cokernels and openness of surjectivity. Nearby zeros over the block stay in those neighborhoods by the same compactness. With this finite-dimensional operator parameter space, the Fredholm implicit function theorem and (2) give local solution manifolds of dimension at most the operator parameter dimension minus one. A generic arbitrarily small parameter misses their projections. Take open chart neighborhoods when applying Sard and then restrict to the compact block. Thus absence is dense for this block even though the individual infinite-jet condition need not be open. Intersect the countably many open dense sets in the smooth constrained parameter space, a Baire space with the usual smooth seminorms. The prescribed kernel line persists by construction and upper semicontinuity on its fixed cover.

Descent and matching

Given any connected finite a:X→Ca:X\to C, pass to a connected normal cover dominating aa and ff and write GG for its deck group and HH for a sheet stabilizer of XX. Pullback identifies the kernel on XX with the HH-invariants in the normal-cover kernel. Conversely a bounded invariant solution descends on the punctured quotient and across its finite branch set by removability for the pulled-back equation. Each irreducible in the real normal-cover kernel defines a twisted solution as above. Removing an ineffective inertia point preserves all such solutions by descent through the corresponding kernel subgroup and removability. Hence the only possible representation is the sign character of ff. Its multiplicity is exactly one: all vectors in its isotypic part are invariant under the kernel of the sign character and descend to YY, where the kernel is the prescribed line. Its HH-invariant space is the line exactly when HH lies in that kernel subgroup, equivalently exactly when aa lifts to YY. This proves (1).

For a nodal stable map to CC apply (1) on each positive normalization. Nonliftable components carry zero height and liftable ones carry a real multiple of the lifted section. On every connected contracted block the operator is the ordinary Dolbeault operator on a trivial vector bundle, and matching makes the height constant across the block. The kernel consists precisely of assignments of these heights agreeing at the nodes, including two flags on the same normalization. Thus at this central operator every nonzero positive image lies on a real dilation of the original graph. Distinct dilations can meet over lower ramification points. Their incidence and localized Euler weights still require a gluing calculation in each degree and genus under study.

First joins in higher degree

Theorem. Suppose two lower sheet values form a complex frame on a regular disk. At every ordinary cubic crossing on a generic path this conclusion holds and evaluation on VV is real injective at every regular value of the cubic. Write b=2lb=2l for its number of simple branch values and Hd=1+d(g−1)H_d=1+d(g-1). In degrees dd indivisible by three the following consequences hold for the connected local changes and, at super-rigid endpoint germs, for the geometric elementary exponents.

  • At an unramified crossing the change vanishes in every genus.
  • At a ramified crossing the change vanishes in every genus for d=1,2,4,5d=1,2,4,5. For larger dd indivisible by three it vanishes in every genus k<Hd+3l+1k<H_d+3l+1. This bound is attained by the central kernel incidence. The Euler weight at equality is undetermined.

Both vanishing statements are coefficientwise local assertions. Intervals and choices of super-rigid ends can be made for each finite list of coefficients as in Article IV, Appendix E.

For each compact chart of effective branch data choose the test point in the subdisk away from its branch positions, refining charts when necessary. Evaluation at the branch values

The marked two-difference evaluation on the ordinary cubic incidence in Article IV, §2 is submersive, including at an arbitrary regular marked base point. In a local labeling its two differences are invertible real linear combinations of two independent conjugate sections in the abstract plane VV. Real rank one for their values in NxN_x has real codimension three in the space of pairs of four-vectors. Rank zero has codimension eight. Allowing the regular point to move adds two real dimensions to the zero-dimensional crossing incidence along a path. Transversality to both rank strata therefore gives real rank two at every regular value on a generic path. Compact exhaustions away from the branch values suffice. Existence of a disk of complex independence is the separate fixed-mark result of Article IV, §2. Transfer of the constrained exclusions to the continued crossing charts then uses the time cutoff argument of Article IV, Appendix E, since the normalized transverse kernel and cubic cover continue uniquely. If a particular graph is prescribed, the evaluation ranks are hypotheses on that graph.

At a ramification point of ZZ, inertia is generated by a transposition. The evaluation V→NxV\to N_x annihilates its negative eigenline. Its rank is exactly one. Indeed the three sheet heights there are v,v,−2vv,v,-2v, and embeddedness of the graph on YY implies v≠0v\ne0 by separation of the two points in the cubic fiber. The negative eigenline consists of the multiples of a root such as (1,−1,0)(1,-1,0) in the sum-zero plane. Each nonzero vector on it has trivial stabilizer as a vector because its three coordinates are distinct. A nonzero vector with transposition stabilizer has two equal coordinates.

It follows that every nonzero component factors through a cubic quotient Z/⟨τ⟩Z/\langle\tau\rangle or through ZZ itself. More precisely, its coefficient vector is fixed by the image of its sheet stabilizer, so the component factors through the quotient of ZZ by the stabilizer of that vector. The resulting degree over CC is divisible by three. If the section has a zero then a branch value is necessary and its coefficient is on a negative eigenline there. The component factors through ZZ and has degree divisible by six. Projectivization does not enlarge the vector stabilizer used in the descent of a section. In the unramified case, real injectivity on every fiber embeds each nonzero orbit multisection, and images of different orbits are disjoint. Matching on a connected domain then confines the whole graph to one such cubic or sextic curve.

The first possible joins outside degree divisible by three

For a connected stable map with nonzero normal kernel and 3∤d3\nmid d, some positive component has zero height, since the sum of the degrees of nonzero components is divisible by three. By connectedness a nonzero positive component must meet height zero, directly or through a constant contracted block. At an unramified crossing this is impossible. At a ramified crossing it requires at least one component factoring through ZZ, and also a zero-height positive component. This excludes d<7d<7.

There are three simple ramification points of ZZ above every lower branch value, so g(Z)=H6+3lg(Z)=H_6+3l. For a component of degree 6e6e factoring through ZZ, Riemann–Hurwitz gives genus at least H6e+3elH_{6e}+3el. Every other positive component of degree jj has genus at least HjH_j. If there are n≥2n\ge2 positive components, adding genera gives k−Hd≥3el+n−1≥3l+1k-H_d\ge 3el+n-1\ge3l+1. At equality one has e=1e=1, n=2n=2, no further ramification, no contracted genus, and no cycle in the dual graph. Stability excludes contracted rational vertices in a tree with only two positive vertices. Hence the source is ZZ joined at a single node to a connected unramified degree-(d−6)(d-6) cover. Its height on ZZ lies on the negative eigenline at the joining flag. Conversely these maps have a kernel for every allowed dd at this genus, by taking a ramification point of ZZ and a preimage of its value on the chosen unramified cover.

Absence of a central projective kernel on the compact fixed-degree, fixed-genus stable-map space implies local constancy of the connected coefficient. For the exponent use the geometric endpoint recursion of Article III, §3. Every divisor of a degree indivisible by three is again indivisible by three. In the unramified case induct first on degree, then on genus. In the ramified case a proper divisor at which a change can occur has excess at least 3l+13l+1, and its jj-fold multiple starts at excess at least j(3l+1)j(3l+1) for j≥2j\ge2. This proves the asserted primitive vanishing through the indicated open range, as well as in all genera for d=1,2,4,5d=1,2,4,5. For two lower branch values over a genus-two curve, the first possible genus in degree seven is twelve. At equality the same proper-divisor bound shows that the primitive change equals the connected change whenever the latter is compared at super-rigid ends. Computing that common value requires the local wall degree of the sextic join.

The first line measures matching after moving the attaching mark and varying the normalized height. The quotient line measures the obstruction on the cubic left by its branch motions. Determining the signed degree still requires the smoothing parameter in both equations, with control of the errors after eliminating the nodal directions.

Local degree and the sum over one branch value

Fix a uniformizing ball in the finite-map chart about each central map, with disjoint images for inequivalent data. The kernel is a line at its center. Stabilization by representatives of PP gives an equivariant line bundle and its obstruction column over a smaller ball times a time interval. The line can be equivariantly trivialized with the action on KK. The column is continuous across the node and smooth on the fixed stratum, where it is the normalized smooth-cover column above. For the continuity one can use thick stabilizing forms and the pullback-family construction of Bai–Swaminathan, Appendix B, or the local polynomial-frame construction of Article IV, §§2–3 and Appendices A–B. The latter has a single cubic nodal factor here, along with smooth quadratic and étale factors; each can be trivialized separately on its source neighborhood. Equivariant averaging of a finite supplement and selection of a minimal invariant complement give the single column. No derivative transverse to q=0q=0 is required.

At time zero the boundaries of the balls are free of kernels by the central classification. Choose the comparisons sufficiently short that their lateral boundaries remain kernel-free. Choose both ends injective at the degree and genus in question. Such ends can be taken arbitrarily close on opposite sides on generic paths, or by arbitrarily small path perturbations preserving the central data and its first derivative as in Article IV, Appendix E. The complement of these neighborhoods is kernel-free on a sufficiently short comparison by compactness at the given degree and genus. The resulting closed cylinder in each uniformizing chart has nonzero column on its whole boundary. Its fixed zero is unique and transverse by the preceding derivative and the inverse function theorem, after shrinking the ball and interval.

The mod-two degree on this boundary is one. Indeed the source and target of the column are isomorphic as real involution representations. Near the unique fixed zero one may extend its fixed derivative by any isomorphism of the moving parts, equivariantly deforming the column in the interior while preserving its fixed restriction there. It can then be perturbed transversely off the fixed set, where additional zeros occur in free pairs. Equivalently this is the mod-two fixed-point formula for the local degree. On the boundary the endpoint-type cokernel bundle is the quotient of PP by the nonzero column line. Upstairs it is the pullback of the tangent bundle to the even sphere S6b+4S^{6b+4} under the normalized column. Its Euler number is twice the signed Brouwer degree, up to the determinant orientation. Integration over the chart quotient divides by two. The localized change is consequently odd. This calculation is the link argument of Article IV, Appendix B with its fixed derivative enlarged by the discriminant pole columns. It also proves invariance of the parity under shrinking the comparison with injective boundary.

At xx the number of join charts is the number of based index-mm subgroups of π1(C,x)\pi_1(C,x), meaning actual subgroups with no conjugacy quotient. For each isomorphism class of unpointed connected cover uu, there are m/|Aut⁡C(u)|m/|\operatorname{Aut}_C(u)| inequivalent choices of a point. Thus modulo two the subtotal is the parity of the index-mm subgroup count. It is odd exactly for a square or twice a square by Müller and Schlage-Puchta, Theorem 1. Multiplying by b=2lb=2l gives even parity for the full change. Since 3∤d3\nmid d, every divisor of dd is also indivisible by three. The lower-genus vanishing and proper-divisor bound of Calculation H1 identify the full connected change here with the primitive change at super-rigid ends. The per-branch subtotals concern localized Euler pairings; the exponent comparison applies after summing. The chart proof works simultaneously at all finitely many flags for each specified dd. No common interval over the infinitely many degrees is asserted.

Genus two on the spin comparison path

Take the repeated and distinct non-effective even-spin endpoints of Article IV, §3.3 on the same genus-two base. That comparison gives a signed count of 3232 ordinary cubic crossings with exactly two simple branch values. Impose the additional residual regularity above on the same path with fixed endpoints. Each such cubic produces two inequivalent degree-seven genus-twelve central maps, one over each value. Hence there are at least 64 distinct pairs of a nodal map and a parameter with odd localized Euler change in arbitrarily small comparison neighborhoods. The cubic can be recovered from the sextic normalization as the isomorphism class of its reflection quotient, so counting distinct cubics introduces no multiplicity here. This counts local contributions and allows cancellation in the total degree-seven invariant. In every degree 6+m6+m with 3∤m3\nmid m, the corresponding statement per branch holds at genus H6+m+4H_{6+m}+4. In particular the two branch values of each cubic have odd subtotals for m=j2m=j^2 or 2j22j^2 with 3∤j3\nmid j.

Signed degree and unramified zero components

Consider the straight-line homotopy from FF to the right side of (3) with q‾\bar q replaced only in the matching term by Q‾\bar Q. Any sequence of noncentral zeros converging to the origin along this homotopy satisfies |h|=O(|Q|)|h|=O(|Q|) by (4) and injectivity of JJ. If q=0q=0 the nodal derivative excludes a noncentral zero. Otherwise project first to P/im⁡JP/\operatorname{im}J, divide by |Q||Q|, and use (4); a limiting unit direction of qq must be in ker⁡A\ker A. Applying Λ\Lambda and dividing by |q||q| in (5) gives the same direction in ker⁡H\ker H. This contradicts (2). Thus the full chart has an isolated zero and its degree is that of this model. Replacing the positive logarithmic factor by one preserves the boundary degree since (2) excludes noncentral model zeros at every positive factor. The Euler number on the link is twice this signed degree and the inertia group has order two, as in Calculation H2. This proves (3).

For different pointed uu the normalized obstruction space and both displayed projections have the same description. In the nodal matching presentation the zero component is invertible and its normalized solution is identically zero as the sextic and the mark vary. Different splittings of the matching sequence or choices of thick forms only change the eliminated block by a shear. More explicitly, JJ projected to the normalized cokernel is the common sextic derivative on branch and time variables; it has image of codimension one and is injective there on those variables. The two attaching columns have zero normalized projection and give vpvp in matching. Thus entries from the branch and time columns into matching do not affect the determinant, by the block determinant with (2). The deformation spaces for the joins have the same complex-oriented branch, attaching and smoothing parameters. The normalization determinant is det⁡DZ⊗det⁡DU⊗(det⁡ℝNx)*\det D_Z\otimes\det D_U\otimes(\det_{\mathbb R}N_x)^* with the complex comparison orientation. The sole change of absolute sign from the identity zero component is ϵ(u*D)ϵ(D)\epsilon(u^*D)\epsilon(D). Summation over m/|Aut⁡u|m/|\operatorname{Aut}u| pointed orbits and then over the bb branch values gives (1). Compactness and the lower-genus and proper-divisor bounds are exactly those in Calculation H1. In particular the isolated charts exhaust the first possible change.

Regularity of the two forms

The nonzero conditions e∉ℂve\notin\mathbb Cv and B(0)v∉ℂvB(0)v\notin\mathbb Cv hold at every marked ramified cubic on a generic path. For the first, use Calculation H2. For the second, augment the joint marked value-difference and derivative test on the cubic by the value of the antilinear coefficient at the base point. Disk-supported variations off the marks kill the annihilating adjoint off the marks. Pure holomorphic jets with independently prescribed marked values and derivatives kill the marked multipliers, since both tests annihilate pulled-back base sections. Elliptic regularity then kills the adjoint across the marks, and free coefficient variation at xx kills its multiplier. This is the marked test of Article IV, §2 with the coefficient evaluation of Article IV, §§2–3 and Appendices A–B. For v≠0v\ne0 the excluded projection of BvBv has real codimension two. The real hyperplane ℝe+ℂv\mathbb R e+\mathbb C v contains just one complex line, ℂv\mathbb C v. Hence AA has real rank one. Choose β≠0\beta\ne0 in its real kernel.

We prove H(β)≠0H(\beta)\ne0 after a generic small disk perturbation preserving the prescribed graph and its branch jets. The resulting smooth-section-plus-poles operator has kernel exactly the prescribed line and cokernel ℝψ\mathbb R\psi by WfW_f. The off-pole image is O(1+|log⁡|w||)O(1+|\log|w||) and lies in every finite LtL^t; the logarithm cancels the 1/w‾1/\bar w forcing. Pairing its image with ψ\psi gives −πRe⁡ψ(0)(R)-\pi\operatorname{Re}\psi(0)(R) by the same boundary integral. Per choice of frames this defines a smooth one-real-column family (a change with the same residue changes the correction by a regular Sobolev section, or one may keep the local choices fixed). Quotient the regular domain by the known kernel line. The resulting operator has index zero. Its invertibility is equivalent to H(β)≠0H(\beta)\ne0, and its kernel and cokernel when defective have dimension one.

Use the disk of complex independence of two cubic sheet heights s1,s2s_1,s_2 to vary the operator by real tensors killing both. In particular all poles, residues, and β\beta are fixed. On the punctured Galois closure a prospective extra polar solution has three conjugate sections h1,h2,h3h_1,h_2,h_3. Its new residue must be nonzero. At each of the three flags over xx, precisely one conjugate has order z−2z^{-2} with nonzero coefficient; its logarithm has lower order. The others have at most simple poles. Thus the three conjugates and the two bounded standard sections have linearly independent real solution germs on the disk by unique continuation. At a Petri jet the following adjoint test applies. An annihilator of the disk variations gives ∑hi⊗ψi=∑j=12sj⊗αj\sum h_i\otimes\psi_i=\sum_{j=1}^2 s_j\otimes\alpha_j, where the ψi\psi_i are the three local adjoint components. Pairing this equality with [D,Φ][D,\Phi] for compactly supported complex-linear Φ\Phi shows the αj\alpha_j solve the adjoint equation, since Φs1,Φs2\Phi s_1,\Phi s_2 are arbitrary independent test sections. The Petri jet and independence of the five germs force the adjoint jets to vanish. Unique continuation gives zero adjoint. The density of a Petri jet under these two prescribed sections, by a local complex gauge and cutoff, is proved in Calculation H1 using Wendl, Corollary 5.10.

Approximate first by a constrained operator with this jet. At any remaining defect the test gives a perturbation with nonzero kernel-to-cokernel derivative for the index-zero quotient. A small multiple removes its simple kernel. This proves open density with fixed graph and fixed AA. The finitely many marked conditions can be imposed simultaneously. For unrestricted generic paths, each normalized transverse crossing continues uniquely on a marked Hurwitz–path chart. The regularity conditions on these finite tests are open, and density on the chart follows by a time cutoff of the graph-preserving perturbations. A countable cover of the crossing incidence by such continuation charts gives the residual path statement as in Article IV, Appendix E. Intersect with the central classification and discriminant regularity of Calculation H2. This proves the stated generic signed result.
